To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The use of a web-based supermarket intervention, which included the introduction of taxes, subsidies, or both for a variety of foods, was associated with significant reductions in the purchase of unhealthy food items and increases in the purchase of healthy food items.

a) the effects of taxes and subsidies on food purchases are highly variable, b) taxes on foods that have a low nutritional value and are consumed frequently (e.g. chocolate bars, potato chips, sugary drinks) are more likely to reduce consumption of those foods compared to subsidies, and c) the effects of food taxes are greater than the effects of food subsidies.

(1) a web-based supermarket intervention can be an effective means of increasing fruit and vegetable consumption; (2) a web-based intervention can be used to test various strategies to promote fruit and vegetable consumption (e.g., taxes, subsidies and both taxes and subsidies); and (3) the use of both taxes and subsidies is an effective means of promoting fruit and vegetable consumption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of various strategies for changing the prices of foods and beverages on the food choices of consumers in an online supermarket.

the effects of food prices on the consumption and purchasing behavior of a large number of households, and the implications of these effects for the health of the population and for the design of public policy.
the effects of food prices on food purchases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a tax on sugary beverages would be a good idea, as would a subsidy for healthy foods.
the evidence from randomized controlled trials and observational studies is not sufficient to support a recommendation for or against the use of a food price policy to improve the diet.

the evidence from the studies included in this systematic review is insufficient to determine whether or not food pricing strategies are effective in reducing the purchase and consumption of unhealthy foods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a healthy eating program can help people to eat healthier and to lose weight.
we have developed a new method for the study of food pricing strategies in randomized controlled trials, and that this method is valid, reliable, and useful in the study of food choices.
the results of our study suggest that the use of a food price strategy in the context of a web-based supermarket is a feasible method for changing dietary behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of food pricing strategies depend on the baseline prices in the market.
the most effective way of improving diet quality is to introduce both taxes and subsidies.
we should be cautious about using food taxes and/or subsidies in isolation as a means to improve dietary patterns.
